intentions.title: Support cross-field validation rules declared as inert JSON data, never as evaluated code
intentions.evidence: rule.ex moduledoc cites locked Decision D7 ('.doey/plans/masterplan-20260425-085425.md'): 'There is NO Code.eval_*, no Code.string_to_quoted + eval, no macro evaluation.' Rules.compile/1 turns JSON like {"when":{"path":"/format","op":"eq","value":"epub"},"then":{"path":"/isbn","op":"nonempty"}} into a plain %Rule{} struct; Evaluator/Ops interpret it recursively rather than executing generated code.

intentions.title: Let a schema author express when/then business rules (e.g. 'ISBN required for epub format') without writing Elixir
intentions.evidence: Rules.compile/1 documented example maps a JSON rule (name/severity/message/tags/when/then) into a compiled Rule; docs/contracts/schema-v2.md is cited as the declared shape; Evaluator.run/3 applies a schema's compiled rules to a document and returns bucketed errors/warnings/infos with concrete paths and messages.

intentions.title: Evaluate validation rules over nested/array content via JSON-Pointer paths with wildcard fan-out
intentions.evidence: Path.resolve/2 supports RFC6901-style paths ('/foo', '/foo/0', '/foo/*', '/items/*/tags/*'), decodes ~0/~1 escapes, and expands `*` into one {concrete_path, value} tuple per array element so a rule like 'every item needs a tag' can be expressed once and checked against every element, substituting integer indices back into violation paths.

intentions.title: Scope rule execution by pipeline stage (live edit vs mutate vs export) so expensive or intrusive rules don't run everywhere
intentions.evidence: Rule.tags is a MapSet of :live/:mutate/:export; Evaluator.run/3 takes a `tag` argument and applies_to_tag?/2 filters rules with a non-empty tag set to only fire for the matching stage — an empty tag set means 'run always'.

intentions.title: Keep the compiled-rule cache correct and fast under a tenant-scoped, low-write-rate schema store
intentions.evidence: Rules is a GenServer holding schema_id -> [Rule.t()] in a plain map (ETS explicitly rejected 'to guarantee consistent ordering with future PubSub-driven invalidation'); put/invalidate/clear/reload_all funnel all mutation through one process while for_schema/1 stays a single GenServer.call on the hot path, sized for '~tens of schemas × tens of rules' with '100+ rule evaluations per pass' being negligible against call overhead.

intentions.title: Make individual rule/checker failures fail closed (rule doesn't fire) rather than crashing document validation
intentions.evidence: Ops.eval/3 catch-all returns false for unknown ops ('Unknown ops return false rather than raising — invalid rules are inert'); {:matches, name} dispatch wraps the checker call in try/rescue and treats any exception or unknown registry lookup as false; Rules.load_from_db/0 wraps DB/compile failures in rescue blocks returning %{} or [].

intentions.title: Provide an extensible custom-checker plugin point (matches:<name>) so schema-specific validators (e.g. codelist_ref, ISBN format) can be added without touching the evaluator
intentions.evidence: Ops.eval({:matches, name}, lhs, args) defers to Barkpark.Validation.Registry.find/1 and calls mod.check(lhs, args); Evaluator moduledoc documents the WI3 handshake: 'registers a codelist_ref checker into Registry... op: "matches:codelist_ref"... No change to this evaluator is required,' establishing checkers as the sanctioned extension seam.
